pick.name: Hinge Health, Inc.
pick.thesis: Ranked first among today's eligible candidates on operating margin trend, six-month return against its sector, six-month return against spy — revenue +49.8% over the trailing year, growth accelerating against the previous quarter, operating margin wider than a year ago, earnings fully backed by cash.

evidence.label: Earnings yield / free cash flow yield
evidence.period: trailing year against the reference close

pick.peerBasis: 113 candidates in SIC major group 73, compared on free cash flow yield, all from the same source and the same periods.

runnersUp.name: Travere Therapeutics, Inc.
runnersUp.why: its weakest signal was growth acceleration (-1.29)

runnersUp.name: Oscar Health, Inc.

runnersUp.name: Madison Square Garden Sports Corp.

pick.counterargument: It is an expensive stock: 75.0× trailing earnings and a 3.5% free cash flow yield, so the growth is already in the price and one weak quarter would cost a lot.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +47.2%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $62.16 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 100 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 100 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-08.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-11-04) plus 364 days

pick.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
pick.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

sources.fundamentals: SEC Financial Statement Data Sets (twelve quarters), point-in-time by accepted timestamp, topped up from companyfacts for companies that have filed since the newest data set
sources.prices: Massive (Polygon.io) grouped daily bars, splits and dividends

stories.title: After losing ground with Latino voters, Democrats are turning to influencers for help
stories.excerpt: Democrats are hoping to win back Latino voters who have soured on both parties. They hope Latino content creators will bridge the gap.
stories.lead:
Democrats lost the 2024 elections in part because of their eroding support among Latino voters, a constituency that was once a reliable segment of their base.

That November, Kamala Harris won the Latino vote by three points, according to the Pew Research Center. In 2020, Joe Biden carried them by 25 points.

This year, swing districts with large Hispanic populations could help decide which party controls the House. And Democrats are scrambling for ways to win those voters back.

stories.title: Rogue Anthropic AI agent gave police fake tip in unsolved murder case
stories.excerpt: Philadelphia police said the tip was "flagged as spam", but criticised the tech company for taking more than two months to detect and report the breach.
stories.lead:
An artificial intelligence (AI) agent, developed by Anthropic, went rogue and sent US police a fake tip about an unsolved murder earlier this year, authorities have revealed.

In a statement police said that the bogus tip came through a public website where people can share information on unsolved murders, and that the AI agent had written that it may have information on a case, and claimed to have seen "someone matching the description".

stories.title: Public executions in the US stopped nearly a century ago - why are they resuming now?
stories.excerpt: The Pentagon says the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan will be livestreamed, but experts suggest officials are reading the country wrong.
stories.lead:
They came in their thousands from near and far. Men, women and children lined up on a Kentucky riverfront for the public hanging of a black man convicted of raping and killing an elderly white widow.

It was 14 August 1936 in Owensboro, Kentucky, a sweltering Friday in the middle of a legendary heat wave. Some slept overnight near the gallows to preserve their spots. Others held "necktie" parties the previous evening, arriving hungover as teenagers sold popcorn and soda to the spectators.

By the execution time of 5am, the crowd had swelled to an estimated 20,000.
